body:
On a Pixel 11 Pro (PowerVR C-Series CXTP-48-1536 MC1, `VK_DRIVER_ID_IMAGINATION_PROPRIETARY`, driver 1.662.3024, subgroup size 128), the IQ quantization types give different results on consecutive runs of the same binary with the same input.

`test-backend-ops test -b Vulkan0 -o GET_ROWS`, three runs back to back:

```
102/115 tests passed
 99/115 tests passed
100/115 tests passed
```

`test-backend-ops test -b Vulkan0 -o MUL_MAT -p type_a=iq2_xxs,`, two runs:

```
14/27 tests passed
15/27 tests passed
```

Every failing case is an IQ type: IQ1_S, IQ1_M, IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ2_S, IQ3_S. IQ3_XXS, IQ4_XS and IQ4_NL pass. Errors are large, around 2.0 for GET_ROWS.

This is not general flakiness on the device. Q4_K passes 26/26 and Q6_K 11/11 across four consecutive runs, and F32/F16 and the legacy quants are stable too.

Varying results from identical input suggests a race or uninitialized memory rather than an arithmetic bug in the shader. The IQ dequant shaders are the ones that index large constant lookup tables, which is the obvious difference from the types that are stable, though I have not confirmed that is the mechanism.

Runs were made with the fix from https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28341 applied, which changes which reduction variant the IQ mul_mat_vec pipelines use. `GET_ROWS` does not go through that path, and it failed the same way before that fix (92/115 on the first run I have), so the two are unrelated.

This may be a driver bug rather than anything in ggml. Filing it because the non-determinism is worth knowing about, and because I have not seen it reported for other backends.

Same device as #28214, different symptom.
title: Vulkan: IQ-type results are not reproducible run to run on Imagination PowerVR
